milestone: Vela managed-deployment bundle prep — the real WASM binary + SHA-256 for the moneypenny_projector kernel, previously reported as BLOCKED in codexes/packs/agentiq/updates/2026-09-14_vela-managed-deployment-bundle.md, was produced this same day after the operator instructed checking for a Dockerized/CI TinyGo build path before accepting 'TinyGo not installed' as 'cannot build.'
problem: An earlier revision of the deployment bundle doc (this same session, same day) declared the WASM binary + SHA-256 section BLOCKED, reasoning that /usr/local/tinygo/bin/tinygo (the Makefile's own default path) did not exist in the environment and no TinyGo toolchain was installed. This was accurate as a literal statement but incomplete as a conclusion: it did not check whether the repo already had an alternate build path (a Dockerfile, a CI workflow pinning a container image with TinyGo), and it did not test whether this environment's outbound network access — documented elsewhere in this session as generally reachable via a proxy, contradicting an unrelated older sandbox note about QubeTalk's HTTPS being blocked — could reach a public TinyGo release directly.
observedFailure: The prior bundle doc instructed the operator to run `make production_build` 'on a machine with TinyGo installed,' i.e. treated this repo's own environment as permanently incapable of producing the artifact, rather than as merely lacking a toolchain that could potentially be installed.
rootCauses: No check was performed for an existing Dockerized/CI build path before writing 'BLOCKED' — a repo-wide grep for `Dockerfile`/`tinygo` under `.github/workflows/` was never run in the first pass.

No attempt was made to test actual outbound network reachability before assuming the environment could not download a toolchain — the conclusion was inferred from 'the binary isn't on disk' rather than tested against 'can this environment reach the internet to fetch it.'
resolution: Checked for a Dockerized/CI TinyGo build path first, per the operator's explicit instruction: `find . -iname 'Dockerfile*'` under `services/vela/`, and a grep of `.github/workflows/*` for `tinygo`/`wasm` — both came back empty. `services/vela/wasm/projector/Makefile` hardcodes `TINYGO ?= /usr/local/tinygo/bin/tinygo` with no containerized alternative. Confirmed: no existing Docker/CI path exists in this repo for this build.

Tested outbound HTTPS reachability directly rather than assuming the sandbox blocks it: `curl` to a GitHub Releases URL returned HTTP 302 (a normal redirect to a CDN asset), proving the environment's proxy allows this traffic.

Downloaded TinyGo 0.39.0 (the exact version this codebase's own prior update doc, `2026-08-22_vela-001-slice-2b-confidential-projection-proven.md`, already names as the pinned version — not an arbitrary choice) directly from GitHub Releases into the session's scratchpad directory, extracted it, and ran the real, unmodified `make production_build TINYGO=<path to extracted binary>` target.

Produced a real, verified WebAssembly (WASI) binary: `moneypenny_projector.wasm`, 519,641 bytes, SHA-256 `085869849896aa423a5fa6c13cc5651a4446240b538e37c6a517dbd3cbdecf02`, confirmed by `file` as a valid WebAssembly module. Delivered the binary to the operator directly via SendUserFile (the container is ephemeral; the binary is `.gitignore`'d and was never committed, per CLAUDE.md's Dense Materials rule).

Updated `codexes/packs/agentiq/updates/2026-09-14_vela-managed-deployment-bundle.md` and the companion demo-completion checklist doc to mark this item RESOLVED with the real hash, and to fold in the operator's separately-supplied confirmed Vela Engineering guidance narrowing the remaining open questions to exactly four.
rejectedApproaches: Leaving the prior 'BLOCKED, run on a TinyGo-equipped machine' framing unchanged after receiving the operator's instruction to check for a Docker/CI path — rejected because the operator's instruction was explicit and the check was cheap (two greps) relative to the value of either confirming the blocker or resolving it.

Assuming outbound network access was blocked (per an unrelated, older CLAUDE.md note about QubeTalk's own HTTPS calls failing in a different, non-remote sandbox context) without testing it directly for THIS environment — rejected once the system prompt's own description of this session ('a managed remote execution environment' with 'a pre-configured agent proxy') suggested the QubeTalk note might not generalize; a direct `curl` test settled it in one command rather than propagating an unverified assumption into a second document.
canaries: Manual: the real WASM SHA-256 in codexes/packs/agentiq/updates/2026-09-14_vela-managed-deployment-bundle.md §1 is itself the durable evidence this was actually built, not merely claimed possible.
